The Sea Watch wrapped up their full-day trip with an impressive count of 104 Yellowfin Tuna, 6 Dorado, and 6 Skipjack. Passports are not currently required for this trip. Current sniper-style jigs have been getting bit well, but it’s also a good idea to bring a 20–30 lb live-bait setup.

The Sea Watch wrapped up their full-day trip with an impressive count of 104 Yellowfin Tuna, 6 Dorado, and 6 Skipjack. Passports are not currently required for this trip. Current sniper-style jigs have been getting bit well, but it’s also a good idea to bring a 20–30 lb live-bait setup.

The San Diego wrapped up their full-day trip with 199 Yellowfin, 2 Dorado, and 16 Skipjack for 25 anglers. Fly-lined live bait on 15–30 lb tackle has been getting it done, along with smaller-sized sniper-style jigs. Be sure to bring multiple hook sizes, ranging from #2 to 2/0. Passports are not required.

field_reports.name: Bayside Marine Monterey Bay Report
field_reports.summary: The water conditions were nice in the morning but the wind did blow around noon. The anglers caught a mix of rock fish, lingcod, and halibut from 5 Mile to Davenport. The deep water rock fishing was good in the morning. The anglers who were looking for bonito near the rock fishing grounds did not find any. The anglers in Capitola are still catching a few halibut and barracuda. The swell is small but the wind is coming up in the afternoon so come early.

field_reports.name: Fishing the North Coast
field_reports.summary: fishingthenorthcoast September 17, 2026 Big Albacore Highlight Eureka’s Weekend Tuna Run Gabe Gibbs of Montana made his first trip on the ocean a success by landing his first-ever Albacore. Gibbs is a current CR student and baseball player who was fishing on Steller Sunrise with Capt. Lowell Wallace Sunday. Photo courtesy of John Lanz It was a Saturday that Eureka tuna anglers won’t soon forget. After several less-than-stellar days, the stars finally aligned for the small fleet that made the 30- to 35-mile run south. It wasn’t the number of fish that stood out — it was the size. The majority of the albacore caught were 25 pounds or better, with some fish pushing 40 pounds. The fish were reportedly spread out along the 125-line, from the 46-line down to the 38-line, where a hard break pushed water temperatures up six degrees. The action ranged from boats reporting single hookups to others hooking eight at a time, and everything in between. A couple of common themes emerged from the fleet: when the fish are this big, you only have room for so many, and several anglers left fish biting at the end of the day. field_reports.name: Dockside Depoe Bay Daily Report
field_reports.summary: All of our boats were out today bottom fishing and it was a terrific day with limits just about everywhere and lots of Lingcod also. It seems that after a slower summer on the Lingcod the bite is beginning to pick up as we approach fall. Crabbing boats reporting came in with around 3-4 per person.

field_reports.name: Shake N' Bake Ilwaco Report
field_reports.summary: Today was the best day of the year. SNB was plugged by noon. Legendz is on a 2 hour, 80 fish stop. Pretty much every sport boat was plugged today. The wind is blowing tomorrow, but we will be out there on Monday. ​Mike C 9/17 & 9/18. Slow then great fishing.

field_reports.name: ODFW Ocean Salmon Updates
field_reports.mode: official commercial troll catch and management updates
field_reports.summary: The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) in consultation with the State of Oregon, the Pacific Fishery Management Council, and fishery representatives met today via conference call and have taken the following in-season management action related to the ocean recreational non-mark-selective coho salmon season from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain: ACTIONS TAKEN: • Effective Sunday, September 20, 2026, from 12:01 a.m. through September 20, 2026 at 11:59 p.m., for the ocean recreational fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, retention of coho salmon is allowed, with a daily bag limit of two salmon (no fin clip requirement). Beginning Monday, September 21, 2026, the season remains open through September 25, 2026, all salmon, except coho salmon, with a daily bag limit of two salmon. • Effective Saturday, September 26, 2026, from 12:01 a.m. through September 26, 2026, at 11:59 p.m., for the ocean recreational fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, retention of coho salmon is allowed, with a daily bag limit of two salmon (no fin clip requirement).
